design_goal: Give recruiters one place to see everything Para AI knows about a candidate, control what it's allowed to know, and direct its actions across every opportunity that candidate is in, without ever wondering what the AI already did on its own. The default landing view matches the recruiter's actual task (check status, take action), not a data-browsing detour through profile or context first.
constraints: Recruiter retains final say on relationship-sensitive actions
No existing design system to build against — generic interaction patterns used instead of Stillsuit DS v2
One shared candidate record per person (confirmed); this feature coordinates the roles the recruiter personally submitted the candidate to
Cross-recruiter duplicate submission to the same role is platform-prevented and out of scope (confirmed)
Every submission originates from a recruiter's action and consent — Para AI recommends but never auto-submits
A consistent place to review/approve Para AI activity across candidates already exists (confirmed); inline approvals roll up to it and redesigning it is out of scope
Assumes reliable company-to-opportunity mapping; calls are on-platform and transcribed when recorded
No standalone Action Queue destination — approval-required items surface inline within their opportunity row

Entire feature lives on one candidate's page (tabs: Opportunities default, Activity, Profile) plus a persistent Ask Para assistant; broader recruiter dashboards (home, candidates list, all-roles view) are out of scope
Calls happen on-platform and are recorded/transcribed automatically; the per-call 'use for Para AI' toggle is the inclusion decision for a call

Para AI has no page of its own — it lives inline on the candidate page, attributed wherever it appears (persistent indicator + labeled tags), and can take actions from the Ask Para chat behind the same approval gate
success_metrics: Less recruiter time spent coordinating one candidate across roles
Fewer opportunities go stale from missed follow-up
Recruiters keep auto-execution on, not off
Recruiters act on Para AI's recommendations more often than not
Zero relationship-sensitive actions sent without recruiter approval
selected_strategy: Opportunities: candidate-centric parallel-track dashboard as the default landing view, with Profile & Context as a secondary view and Para AI embedded inline rather than siloed in a separate destination
selected_strategy_rationale: The brief's core problem is recruiters reconstructing one candidate's status from scattered per-role views; a single dashboard showing every active opportunity as a parallel track answers that directly, and gives Para AI a natural home for cross-opportunity reasoning like conflict detection. Refined further so this dashboard (not profile or context data) is what a recruiter lands on, and so approval-required Para AI actions appear inline on the opportunity itself rather than behind a separate Action Queue tab — matching where the recruiter's actual task already is.

alternative_strategies.name: Candidate record with opportunity tabs
alternative_strategies.summary: One candidate page, opportunities as tabs within it
alternative_strategies.rejected_because: Tabs only show one opportunity at a time, preserving the fragmentation the feature is meant to solve

tradeoffs: Compact per-opportunity rows can't show full detail without an expand step (drawer)
Requires cross-opportunity data plumbing (company mapping, unified stage model) that may not exist yet
Bulk-approve mitigation reduces but does not eliminate rubber-stamp risk

Removing the separate Action Queue means an approval-required item is only as visible as the row it's attached to — but Paraform already has a consistent cross-candidate Para review surface these roll up to (confirmed), so this is not a coverage gap
assumptions: Resume/LinkedIn default Included in matching; notes/calls default excluded, with a one-tap prompt at capture time
Candidate is never a user of this system, only its subject
One shared candidate record; coordination is scoped to the roles the recruiter personally submitted the candidate to (confirmed)
Every submission originates from a recruiter's action and consent; Para AI recommends but never auto-submits (confirmed)
Context comes from resume/LinkedIn structured insights, recruiter-added preferences, and transcript-derived insights when calls are recorded (confirmed)
The private / include-in-matching control is a NEW distinction this design proposes — Paraform has no such control today (confirmed as a new distinction)
Durable context (resume, tenure history) does not decay; volatile context (preferences, comp, timing) does, and is shown with a staleness indicator past a set age
The cross-opportunity hold and match scores are design proposals, flagged as assumptions
open_issues: Whether the Include-in-matching toggle should default on or off for notes/calls (proposed new control)
Whether a one-tap share prompt at capture is sufficient, or a periodic under-sharing nudge is needed
How Para AI computes the match score on recommended opportunities, and how to keep it legible/trustworthy
Which state changes trigger a cross-opportunity hold (offer confirmed vs. verbal vs. final round) and how long Para holds before re-escalating
Whether a flat 60-90 day staleness threshold is right for all volatile context, or whether different fact types decay at different rates
Whether company-to-opportunity mapping is reliable enough to hard-block same-company double submission, or whether it degrades to a soft warning
How the candidate page hands off to Paraform's existing cross-candidate Para review/approve surface
resolved_by_paraform: One shared candidate record (dropped the earlier per-recruiter-silo assumption)
Coordination is scoped to the recruiter's own submissions
Cross-recruiter duplicate submission is platform-prevented and out of scope
Para never auto-submits — every submission originates from recruiter action/consent
A consistent cross-candidate Para review/approve surface already exists
Context = resume/LinkedIn structured insights + recruiter-added preferences + transcript insights when recorded
Private/exclude-from-Para is a new distinction, not existing behavior
risks: Bulk-approve remains a genuine trust risk even with a forced per-item preview
If underlying cross-opportunity data isn't reliable, conflict-blocking behavior would need to degrade to a manual warning instead of a hard block
A cross-opportunity hold that pauses too aggressively could feel obstructive — the trigger set and hold duration need real-world tuning
A staleness indicator that isn't backed by matching logic actually discounting older signals would mislead recruiters about what Para AI is using, the same trust failure as a false 'undo'
A match score shown without an explanation reads as a black box and can erode trust — it needs a legible 'why'
ds_patterns_used: chat panel with inline action cards
new_patterns_required: persistent Auto vs. Approval-required tag system (no existing precedent since there is no shared design system for this exercise)
inline approval card embedded in a list row (replaces a separate review-queue screen)
cross-opportunity hold card (Para pauses its own actions on other opportunities based on cross-opportunity state)
in-chat action card (Para takes an action from the assistant behind the standard approval gate)
Para AI attribution tag (labels AI-originated content without a dedicated destination)
next_actions: Pressure-test the Opportunities row + inline approval + cross-opportunity hold as one system sharing the act-vs-wait tag language
Decide whether Board (kanban) view needs its own full wireframe or stays a stated capability
